absent: Numeric values and bit positions of balancing flags, migration kinds, idle kinds, break quantum and dequeue and enqueue clock options.
Full memory layouts of the balancing environment, run queue, scheduling domain, task, NUMA group and cache group structures.
Behavior of hierarchical load, estimated utilization, fitness test, throttling test, per CPU thread test, blocked test and running and donor tests not routed here.
Lock ordering and interrupt state when source and destination queue locks are held together and lifetime rules for the collected task list.
Update rules and scaling for shared cache utilization and capacity, preferred cache identifiers, invalid counts and capacity exceed checks.
Configuration conditions selecting between alternate helper variants and feature flags for minimal load, buddy heat and placement lag.
Definitions and ranges of tunable thresholds for migration cost, cache tries, aggregation percentage and imbalance percentage.

findings.text: The routine can_migrate_task is visible outside its file and serves as the eligibility predicate for movement between processors. It consumes a task and a balancing environment and reports allowance while updating pinning and heat markers.

Detachment yields no work when the source queue holds at most one runnable entity or when the requested imbalance is already satisfied. In the single runnable case the all pinned marker is cleared because no candidate was examined.

The charge against the imbalance budget depends on movement kind. Load movement uses hierarchical load floored at one and utilization movement uses estimated utilization, both relaxed by repeated failure count through a bounded shift, while task counting kinds consume one unit per task and misfit movement consumes the whole remainder only for tasks that do not fit the source processor.

Tasks whose allowed processor set excludes the destination are refused and record partial pinning. When the destination group offers another allowed processor and the operation is neither a fresh idle pull nor an active balance nor already redirected, the environment records an alternate destination and a destination pinned marker.

Heat assessment exempts tasks outside the fair class, tasks with idle policy, and domains that share capacity. Otherwise heat follows core cookie compatibility and recency of execution against a tunable cost, with buddy candidacy forcing heat.

Locality degradation is neutral when balancing is disabled, when fault data is absent, when the domain lacks NUMA character, when source and destination share a node, or when the destination is fully idle. Movement away from the preferred node is penalized unless preferred occupancy is low, movement toward it is encouraged, otherwise the outcome compares per mille fault weights of source and destination.

Per node weights combine directly attributed memory faults across both access categories with contributions from nearby nodes. Directly connected topologies add no nearby contribution, backplane topologies restrict contributors by distance limit, and mesh topologies discount distant contributions proportionally to remaining distance.

Cache level capacity fit compares utilization scaled by one hundred against capacity scaled by an over aggregation percentage, enlarged for single thread siblings. One utilization dominates another when it exceeds the other by more than an imbalance percentage.

Cache aware movement is unrestricted when statistics are unavailable, when source and destination share a cache, when no cache group is attached, when thread counts or capacities invalidate grouping, or when neither side can accommodate the task after adjustment. Otherwise preference direction decides whether overload of the preferred side or lack of overload on the source side forbids movement.

Inspection and removal paths require the source queue lock to be held by the caller. Heat evaluation, eligibility evaluation, detachment iteration and single task removal all assert this ownership and must not be invoked without it.

Attachment to the destination acquires and releases the destination queue lock internally and refreshes that queue clock while held. The single task attach helper itself expects the destination lock already held and validates that the task already targets that queue.

The balancing environment carries source and destination queue references and processor numbers, group masks and processor sets, a domain reference, an imbalance budget, loop counters and limits with break spacing, an idle state indicator, a migration kind selector, flag bits for pinning and breaking and active operation, an alternate destination, and a list head for collected tasks.

Observed task state relevant to balancing includes fair entity linkage and delay and eligibility markers, heat and movement counters, affinity mask pointer, scheduling class, execution start stamp, NUMA fault tables and totals with preferred node and group reference, cache group reference with preferred cache identifier, and core cookie.

Detachment operates as a bounded collection with three terminal budgets of total iterations, periodic break spacing that sets a need break marker, and remaining imbalance. Skipped candidates rotate to the tail of the source list while accepted candidates transfer to the collection list, with fresh idle operation stopping after one acceptance on preemptible builds.

Eligibility evaluation maintains heat and pinning markers across calls. It clears the visible heat marker on entry, may set it when a hot task is nevertheless accepted after many failures, and clears the all pinned marker once any task passes affinity while setting some pinned, destination pinned or cache pinned markers on specific refusal causes.

Unbounded stealing risks mutual pilfering and livelock, so idle stealing preserves one runnable entity on the source and fresh idle handling minimizes hold time. Periodic breaking limits continuous list traversal under lock.

Several helpers have build dependent variants that unconditionally disable a check. Throttle hierarchy, locality degradation, cache degradation, wrong destination, cookie matching, core membership and cache statistics each collapse to a constant in one configuration, so callers cannot assume the check is active.

The migration cost control uses two sentinel values. Negative one forces every candidate to be treated as hot and zero forces every candidate to be treated as cold, while positive values act as a time threshold in the same units as the queue task clock.
Statistics collection for gained tasks, hot gains, forced moves and refusal causes is conditional on a global enablement. When disabled the accounting operations have no effect.

Eligibility additionally refuses tasks whose destination group queue sits in a throttled hierarchy, per processor kernel threads, blocked tasks, currently running or donor tasks, delayed dequeued tasks except under load movement, and lag ineligible tasks when placement lag handling is enabled and the destination has queued entities.

Core cookie compatibility is automatic when core scheduling is disabled on the queue or when cookies match or when every sibling thread in the core is idle and not preempted. Otherwise the destination is considered incompatible and forces heat.

Successful removal deactivates the task from the source without clock update and retargets its processor to the destination, recording forced movement when heat was present. Attachment later activates each collected task on the destination without clock update and evaluates preemption with a non waking flag.
